title: Voyager 1 at one light-day: Historian revisits Golden Record's forgotten details
gist: As Voyager 1 reached one light-day from Earth on November 18, historian Glen Swanson shared rediscovered details of the Golden Record: blueprints confirm operating instructions were repeated inside the protective cover, and NASA ordered 10 extra copies whose locations he verified. The findings come from a book with design director Jon Lomberg due from the University of Chicago Press in August 2027.

insights.claim: Glen Swanson found in original blueprints that the Golden Record's designers repeated the playing instructions on the inside of its protective cover, because the outer inscriptions would eventually erode from dust.
insights.speaker: Robert Pearlman
insights.so_what: Illustrates redundancy-by-design thinking for long-duration engineering.
insights.quote: “Even small amounts of dust are eventually going to wear down the inscriptions to the point perhaps where they are not going to be readable.”

insights.claim: Swanson's research focused on the record's hardware rather than its contents, noting existing information is sparse and somewhat contradictory.
insights.speaker: Robert Pearlman
insights.so_what: Archival research can surface new facts about well-known programs.

insights.claim: Swanson and Lomberg's book, Voyager's Golden Record: An Enduring Reflection, will be released by the University of Chicago Press in August 2027, with a non-playable full-size copper record replica planned alongside.
insights.speaker: Robert Pearlman

insights.claim: The Golden Record was initially made in three copies, and about a month after launch NASA approved 10 extras including the spare, though reports have cited between six and 14.
insights.speaker: Robert Pearlman
insights.so_what: Scarcity underpins the artifacts' historic value.

insights.claim: Swanson verified original duplicates at JPL, the United Nations, the Library of Congress, NASA Headquarters, the Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum, and several NASA centers, and believes President Carter likely returned his copy to NASA HQ.
insights.speaker: Robert Pearlman
insights.so_what: Provenance details for historic space artifacts.
